newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ BILL YIELDS RISE AS TWI FALLS AND MCI EASES.
newsitem.headline: NZ BILL YIELDS RISE AS TWI FALLS AND MCI EASES.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 92.06 (PREV 92.10) 90-DAYS 8.27 (PREV 8.21)
OVERNIGHT CASH 8.10 PCT (PREV 8.15) US 5-YR 6.10 (PREV 6.12)
RBNZ MCI NZ/MCI 738.63 (PREV 744.25) Reuters NZ MCI -86 vs -78
The New Zealand bank bill yields rose six basis points on Thursday morning as the currency eased further to loosen the Monetay Conditions Index another couple of notches.
Traders said the market was quiet with the main event being the tender of $150 million of government 7/09 bonds at 1.00 p.m. (0100 GMT).
The short end of the market remains riveted to currency so that where the kiwi goes the bills go.
"There is a bit of bid come into the back of the curve now but the front is currency-watching to an extent," said ANZ Investment Bank's senior domestic markets manager Jim Reardon said.
"No one is panicking to get the MCI into line. The concept of a band at 70 is somewhat lost on the market these days and gradually over time we will continue to see it slip higher."
The MCI was 86 points easier than the RB's desired level from 78 at Wednesday's close.
Reardon picked that by publication time of the Reserve Bank's six monthly economic projections on September 18 the MCI would be 725 (off 100 basis points) or lower.
The $600 million World Bank eurobond issue this week should increase confidence for today's bond tender although liquidity in the 09s remains problematic.
The 09s are quoted around 6.78 percent, six basis points under the 11/06s and that margin is forecast by some traders, but not all, to hold.
"Internationally, people will be eyeing the currency though and wondering whether it is a good entry point," said another bank senior dealer.
He noted that the last tender was taken out by three bidders and by most accounts the bonds now reside offshore.

"For my money there is no illiquidity premium placed on the 09s. I believe a fairer price is they should be flat against the 06s irrespective of the inverse yield curve. There are just none out there."
